title: When Baxter Walked Away From CPAP, Peter Farrell Bought It
conflicts: 1989 money: Farrell (Horatio Alger, 2022) says he raised $1 million from Australian investors; Forbes Australia (2025) says he raised $1 million and paid Baxter $558,000 for the IP; SmartCompany (2013) says $1.25 million of his own money; NHMRC says investors. Story gives Farrell's $1m-from-investors account and the 2013 own-money version, and omits the price. Baxter's involvement dated 1981 (Horatio Alger) vs 1986–87 (ResMed, NHMRC, SmartCompany); story uses 1986. Reasons Baxter withdrew differ (sold respiratory division; 'bigger fish to fry'; too experimental; closed Australian lab); story uses the first two. First patient 1980 vs 1981; story says early 1980s.
notes: Company written as 'ResCare (later ResMed)'. Story centres on Farrell's 1989 decision, with Sullivan's homemade machine as the setup. Eddie's quotation is a patient's words as reported by Forbes Australia. Health-related but talQen not mentioned, as instructed.
